case_name: Duraisami v State of Tamil Nadu
respondent:
State of Tamil Nadu
Supreme Court of India

5 October 2004
Cr.A. No. 355 of 2000
The Order of the Court was as follows:
1.  The appellant was an Assistant Executive Engineer in the Public Works Department at Kangeyam, Periyar district in Tamil Nadu. During the relevant period the appellant was in charge of releasing of water from LBP Dam at Bhavani Sagar Project at Chennanamalai division. The cultivators of that area had grievance that the accused was not releasing sufficient water for irrigation purpose and PW 1 M.Govindasamy alleged that the appellant had demanded Rs.1500/- as bribe for releasing water to the cultivators. He made a complaint and a trap was laid on 16-3-1988. PW 1 gave Rs.500/- to the appellant and the police party who were waiting thereby effected recovery of the alleged tainted amount from the appellant and a case was registered against him.
2. The appellant admitted the receipt of Rs.500/- from PW 1 but he contended that he had sold Indira Vikas Patras
facts: The appellant was an Assistant Executive Engineer in the Public Works Department at Kangeyam, Periyar district in Tamil Nadu.

Cultivators of that area had grievance that the accused was not releasing sufficient water for irrigation purpose and PW 1 M.Govindasamy alleged that the appellant had demanded Rs.1500/- as bribe for releasing water to the cultivators.
The trial court accepted the explanation of the appellant and acquitted him of all the charges framed against him.

The State preferred an appeal before the High Court and the learned Single Judge set aside the acquittal and found the appellant guilty under Section 5(1)(d) read with Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act,1947 and Section 161 IPC
The finding of the learned Single Judge is challenged before us.

The learned Single Judge reversed the acquittal passed by the Special Judge firstly for the reason that the appellant did not give a statement at the time of his arrest that the money he had received was towards the value of two Indira Vikas Patras sold by him to PW 1
Exhibit P-16, communication sent by him to the office of the Executive Engineer, probabilises the version given by the appellant.
He also examined DW 1 and DW 2 to support his case.
issues: What was the understanding of the appellant and PW 1?
Was the evidence of DW 2 justified in rejecting?
petitioner_arguments: The appellant admitted the receipt of Rs.500/- from PW 1 but he contended that he had sold Indira Vikas Patras to PW 1 on 1-12-1987, and for which he had not paid the money
The appellant produced Exhibit P-16, communication sent by him to his immediate superior.
He relied on Exhibit P-16,communication sent by him to the office of the Executive Engineer.
He also examined DW 1 and DW 2 to support his case.
respondent_arguments: The State preferred an appeal before the High Court
The learned Single Judge set aside the acquittal and found the appellant guilty under Section 5(1)(d) read with Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act,1947 and Section 161 IPC
The finding of the learned Single Judge is challenged before us.
court_reasoning: We do not think that the learned Single Judge was justified in rejecting the evidence of DW 2.
Once Exhibit P-16 was found to be a true and genuine document, the case set up by the defence has to be accepted
In that view of the matter we do not think that the learned Single Judge was justified in reversing the acquittal passed by the Special Judge.
holding: We set aside the conviction and sentence of the appellant for the offence punishable under Section 161 IPC and Section 5(1)(d) read with Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act.
The appeal is allowed. The fine, if paid, shall be refunded to the appellant.
